title: Encode a logical superposition
description: A CSS encoding isometry maps |i⟩ into the repetition code while preserving its relative phase. Decoding with its adjoint returns the original state.

title: Build a CSS code from binary checks
description: X and Z checks on all four qubits define a code with two logical qubits and distance two.

title: Prepare a CSS coset state
description: The checks XX and ZZ define a Bell state. The representative 0 selects its uniform superposition over 00 and 11.

title: Paste a Qiskit Pauli label
description: A single-quoted Pauli label with a -1j phase prefix maps |000⟩ to |110⟩ exactly.

title: Correct a detected bit flip
description: The syndrome [1,1] selects a middle-qubit X correction for the repetition code. Applying it restores the encoded superposition; fidelity is one.

title: Find a quantum code's distance
description: The five-qubit code encodes one logical qubit with distance three. The result lists [physical qubits, logical qubits, distance]; it can correct any single-qubit Pauli error.

title: Detect a bit-flip error with stabilizers
description: The repetition-code checks ZZI and IZZ both anticommute with a flip on the middle qubit. Syndrome bits 1,1 mean both stabilizer measurements change sign.

title: Paste a stabilizer group
description: Angle brackets enclose Pauli generators. Adjacent letters inside the group are tensor factors: XX and ZZ stabilize the Bell state Phi+.

title: Paste a LaTeX expectation value
description: The physics-package expval macro evaluates the observable in an explicit state. The +1 eigenstate of Pauli Y is |i⟩, including its complex phase.

title: Build a quantum gate from a binary map
description: The binary map (x0,x1) → (x0,x0 XOR x1) becomes CNOT. Acting on |+0⟩ entangles the qubits; only 00 and 11 are measured.

title: Invert a reversible binary map
description: Invert a linear bit transformation over GF(2). XOR is the addition operation, so the inverse can differ from its ordinary real-valued matrix inverse.

title: Solve Simon measurement equations
description: Measured strings 010 and 101 constrain the hidden mask. Solve their homogeneous equations over GF(2); the nonzero nullspace basis vector is 101. All XOR combinations of basis columns are solutions.

title: Recover a parity mask with XOR
description: The predicate x>=2 xor x mod 2 is the parity of the two input bits. Its phase oracle and two Hadamards recover the mask 11 with ideal probability 1.

title: A compound oracle predicate
description: The predicate x=1 or x=3 marks states whose last bit is 1. Acting on |++⟩ produces |+−⟩; inspect the minus signs in the amplitudes.

title: Grover search with an equality predicate
description: Use x=3 directly as the oracle predicate. It marks the two-qubit state |11⟩; one diffusion step yields that outcome with ideal probability 1.

title: Grover search with a formula-defined phase oracle
description: On two-bit indices, floor(x/3) is 1 only for x=3. The phase oracle marks |11⟩ and one diffusion step amplifies its ideal probability to 100%.

title: Bernstein–Vazirani from an oracle expression
description: Build the parity oracle for hidden string 101 directly from its binary inner-product formula. Hadamards and phase kickback recover 101 on the three input wires.
expression: probs((H @ H @ H @ I)oracle_function(bitdot("101",bits(x,3)),3,1,x)(H @ H @ H @ I)|000,−⟩,[0,1,2])

title: Fixed-width binary registers
description: Convert integer indices to four-bit registers, combine them with XOR, and decode the result. Leading zeros remain part of each vector until it is decoded.

title: Binary oracle identities
description: Entrywise XOR retains leading zeros and the width of each register. Its bit-vector result composes directly with the binary inner product.

title: Binary phase kickback
description: The binary inner product counts overlapping 1 bits modulo 2. Its parity determines the phase sign used in Bernstein–Vazirani and Walsh–Hadamard formulas.

title: Comma-separated input registers
description: A comma inside the ket separates tensor-product registers. The controlled gate turns |+,0⟩ into the correlated Bell state.

title: Bell probability from separate register bras
description: Adjacent output bras and input kets form their respective registers before contracting with the gate. Squaring the 11 amplitude gives the Bell-state outcome probability.

title: Adjacent registers through a controlled gate
description: Adjacent kets form a tensor-product register before the gate acts. CNOT applied to |+⟩|0⟩ prepares Φ+, with correlated 00 and 11 outcomes. Ordinary matrix juxtaposition still multiplies matrices.

title: The Bell singlet
description: Ψ− is the normalized state (|01⟩−|10⟩)/√2. Its computational outcomes are always opposite. Bell labels accept Greek, ASCII, and LaTeX forms with an explicit sign.

title: Fourier transform of a zero register
description: The label 0^3 means three repeated zero bits, equivalent to |000⟩ or |0⟩ tensor-cubed. QFT(3) creates a uniform distribution over its eight basis states.

title: An order-finding orbit in ket notation
description: The orbit of 1 under multiplication by 2 modulo 15 contains 1, 2, 4, and 8. The indexed sum builds its normalized superposition, using the new infix modular notation inside a dimension-qualified ket.

title: Sum over computational basis states
description: A dimension-qualified ket evaluates its index inside the sum. This builds the normalized two-qubit uniform state, equivalent to H⊗H acting on |00⟩. Unsuffixed binary labels keep their leading zeroes.

title: A controlled gate from blocks
description: An indexed direct sum puts I in the control-zero block and X in the control-one block. The result is CNOT, with the first qubit as control. Blocks follow increasing index order.

title: Indexed layer of rotations
description: The finite tensor product puts increasing indices left to right. Ry(2π) contributes a minus sign, so this layer returns −|010⟩. Bounds are inclusive; put the TeX operand in braces.

title: Recover a gate from its logarithm
description: logm uses the natural matrix logarithm, with argument +π at negative real eigenvalues. Exponentiating it reconstructs X, including its global phase. For evolution exp(−iHt), take H=i logm(U) at unit time.

title: Pasted multiplication and division
description: Typographic multiplication and division signs follow the same ordering rules as * and /. This verifies the noncommuting Pauli identity XY=iZ with symbols copied from mathematical text.

title: Pasted square-root notation
description: Unicode radicals accept gates and grouped expressions. Here √SWAP is the same matrix root as sqrt(SWAP), with its principal complex phase retained.

title: A square-root SWAP gate
description: Fractional matrix powers preserve the principal branch and global phase. Applying this root twice gives SWAP; one application entangles the initial product state.

title: Echoed cross-resonance gate
description: ECR uses ordered operands, with the first on the left in tensor products. This checks its exact standard-gate decomposition, including the global phase required when the gate is controlled.

title: Entanglement left after mixing
description: Half a Bell state mixed with uniform noise has negativity 0.125. Unlike marginal entropy, negativity detects entanglement in this mixed state. Subsystem zero is the leftmost qubit.

title: Overlap of operator expressions
description: Double brackets use column-stacked operators. Parentheses let a label contain an expression; this overlap is the Hilbert–Schmidt product Tr(A†A), without normalization.

title: Lindblad relaxation toward the ground state
description: A collapse operator carries the square root of its rate. This unit-rate lowering operator gives the derivative of the excited-state density matrix, gaining ground population and losing excited population.

title: A commutator in operator space
description: spre(A) and spost(A) multiply an operator from the left and right. Their difference implements the commutator in the column-stacking basis.

title: Rotation about an equatorial axis
description: R(theta,phi) rotates through theta about cos(phi)X+sin(phi)Y. At phi=pi/2 it is Ry; both parameters are in radians.

title: A gate controlled by a binary pattern
description: The quoted pattern must contain one bit per control. The leftmost control is the most significant bit; here X activates only when the controls are 01.

title: Chi process matrix of the phase gate
description: The normalized Pauli convention gives E(rho)=sum(chi_ij P_i rho P_j)/d. Complex off-diagonal entries preserve relative phases; this matrix does not compose channels by ordinary multiplication.

title: Inspect one qubit of an entangled pair
description: The optional wire index selects a qubit, with wire 0 leftmost. Each qubit of this pure Bell pair is individually maximally mixed, at the sphere center.

title: A pure state on the Y axis
description: Bloch coordinates are the normalized Pauli X, Y, Z expectations. This expression also opens the sphere view, with vector length and purity.

title: Watch damping move a state inward
description: Amplitude damping reduces Y coherence and moves the state toward +Z, the ground-state pole. The shorter vector indicates a mixed state.

title: Relaxation from T1 and T2
description: Use consistent time units for T1, T2 and elapsed time. At T1=T2=1 and time ln(2), the Y coherence decays to one half.

title: Pauli coordinates of a Y eigenstate
description: paulivec uses the normalized Pauli basis. Multiplying by sqrt(2) gives the familiar augmented Bloch coordinates [1,x,y,z].

title: Reconstruct a noisy state from Pauli coordinates
description: Convert the density matrix to Pauli coordinates, apply a damping PTM, then use unpaulivec to reconstruct the output density matrix.

title: Amplitude damping in the Pauli basis
description: The Pauli transfer matrix uses rows and columns I, X, Y, Z. Its first column shows the shift toward the ground state; the remaining columns describe Bloch-vector contraction.

title: Rotate Bloch coordinates with a phase gate
description: The augmented Bloch vector of |+⟩ is [1,x,y,z]=[1,1,0,0]. The S channel sends it to |i⟩, with y=1.

title: Relax toward a thermal population
description: The optional second parameter is the equilibrium probability of |1⟩. Complete relaxation sends any input to that diagonal mixed state.

title: Combine relaxation and dephasing
description: Amplitude 1/4 and phase damping 1/2 leave half the initial coherence. The third parameter sets the equilibrium excited-state population to 1/4.

title: Energy loss from an excited qubit
description: Amplitude damping with probability 3/4 transfers excited-state population to |0⟩. The constructor returns Kraus matrices for channel().

title: Partial loss of phase coherence
description: Phase damping leaves populations unchanged and scales coherence by sqrt(1-p). At p=3/4 the X expectation of |+⟩ falls to 1/2.

title: Depolarize one half of a Bell pair
description: Applying complete depolarization to wire 0 destroys the Bell correlations. The two-qubit state becomes maximally mixed, with purity 1/4.

title: Pauli ladder combination
description: The imaginary coefficient in iY is multiplied by the Pauli Y matrix. (X+iY)/2 lowers |1⟩ to |0⟩.

title: Operator hats in a matrix element
description: Operator hats preserve the named matrix: the hatted Pauli Y has expectation 1 in |i⟩.

title: Fermionic swap keeps the exchange sign
description: FSWAP exchanges adjacent Jordan–Wigner modes. Swapping two occupied modes adds a minus sign, unlike ordinary SWAP.

title: Jordan–Wigner parity sign
description: Removing the fermion at mode 1 from |110⟩ contributes a minus sign because mode 0 is occupied. Mode 0 is the leftmost bit.

title: Lower a Fock state
description: In a five-level truncation, a|2⟩ = √2|1⟩. Explicit dimension suffixes distinguish occupation numbers from binary qubit labels.

title: The truncation boundary matters
description: The finite-dimensional commutator is I − d|d−1⟩⟨d−1|. Its expectation on the top state is −4 for d=5, not 1.

title: Phase estimation: modular multiplier eigenphase
description: The work register is an eigenstate of multiplication by 2 modulo 15 with eigenvalue i. Controlled powers and an inverse QFT recover phase 1/4 as the counting-register bitstring 01.

title: Order finding: multiply by 2 modulo 15
description: Four modular multiplications return |0001⟩ to itself: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 1. States outside the modulus remain fixed.

title: Deutsch–Jozsa: balanced parity function
description: The truth table 0,1,1,0 is balanced. The input register returns 11, never 00. The final qubit starts in |−⟩ for phase kickback.

title: Grover search: one marked state
description: Two Grover iterations amplify |101⟩ from probability 1/8 to 121/128.

title: Grover search: two marked states
description: One iteration finds either |001⟩ or |110⟩ with certainty. Marked indices are decimal, with the leftmost bit most significant.

title: Choi matrix of complete dephasing
description: The Kraus operators I/sqrt(2) and Z/sqrt(2) give a Choi matrix with trace 2, in input ⊗ output order.

title: Operator double-ket
description: Column-stack the Pauli Y operator into a Liouville-space vector; the signs distinguish this from row stacking.

title: Reorder a qubit and qutrit
description: Move the qutrit before the qubit while preserving the superposition. Output dimensions are [3,2].

title: Entangle two qutrits
description: Fourier preparation followed by modular SUM produces a maximally entangled pair; either qutrit has reduced state I/3.

title: Qutrit cyclic shift
description: An explicit dimension makes |2>_3 a three-level basis vector; shifting wraps it to |0>_3.

title: QFT from elementary gates
description: Two-qubit positive-exponent Fourier transform of |01>, including the final wire swap.

title: Teleport a phase-sensitive qubit
description: Measure Alice's two qubits, apply X/Z corrections to Bob, and trace out Alice. Bob recovers |i>.

title: Nonadjacent wires
description: Control wire 0, target wire 2; the middle wire is untouched.

title: Open control
description: Flip the target when the leading control is zero.

title: Textbook Toffoli
description: C squared means two controls, both activated on 1.

title: U gate state preparation
description: Prepare the +Y eigenstate using a three-angle single-qubit gate.

title: Pauli Hamiltonian
description: Evolve under X for pi/2 with hbar equal to one.

title: Heisenberg singlet energy
description: The singlet has expectation −3 for XX + YY + ZZ.

title: Bell probabilities
description: The outcomes 00 and 11 each have probability one half.

title: Postselect zero
description: Project a plus state onto zero and normalize the branch.

title: Read an output register
description: Measure wires 2 and 0 in that order; the outcome is 01.

title: Phase a density matrix
description: Apply S on the ket and S dagger on the bra.

title: Purity of a reduced Bell pair
description: A globally pure entangled pair has a mixed single-qubit reduction.

title: Reduced Bell state
description: Trace out wire 1 to reveal a maximally mixed qubit.

title: Amplitude damping
description: An excited qubit decays with probability one quarter.

title: Complete dephasing
description: Random I or Z removes coherence from a plus state.

title: Reset one half of a Bell pair
description: Reset wire 0 to zero while preserving the mixed state of wire 1.

title: Bell pair
description: Entangle two qubits with Hadamard and CNOT.

title: Measure a Bell pair without reading the outcome
description: Z-basis measurement removes quantum coherence but preserves the classical Z correlation.

title: Pasted bra-ket expression
description: Evaluate a Y expectation using mathematical TeX.

title: Exchange an excitation with iSWAP
description: The exchanged state gains a relative phase of i.

title: Raise a spin-one magnetic state
description: Basis index 1 is m=0; Jplus raises it to m=1 with coefficient sqrt(2). Units use hbar=1.

title: Spin-three-halves total angular momentum
description: The squared angular momentum has eigenvalue j(j+1)=15/4 in every magnetic state.

title: Spin singlet in arrow notation
description: Up and down denote the Z-basis qubit states 0 and 1. The singlet has zero total z spin.

title: Phase kickback with a compact product ket
description: The XOR oracle applies a sign to odd-parity inputs when the output qubit starts in |−⟩.

title: Entropy of one half of a Bell pair
description: The reduced qubit is maximally mixed and has one bit of von Neumann entropy. Density-matrix entropy is numerical.

title: Distinguish a pure qubit from a mixed qubit
description: Trace distance is zero for identical states and one for perfectly distinguishable states. It is evaluated numerically.

title: Squared fidelity of noncommuting mixed qubits
description: Fidelity uses the squared convention, matching Qiskit state_fidelity. These mixed states point along different Bloch axes.

title: Bell state by an even-parity rotation
description: Rotate |00⟩ into an equal, positive superposition with |11⟩.

title: Schmidt coefficients of an unequal pair
description: The coefficients describe entanglement across the first qubit versus the rest. The input is normalized automatically.

title: Trace norm of a gate
description: Indexed norm bars use the Schatten convention: 1 is trace, 2 is Frobenius, infinity is spectral.

title: A matrix norm pasted from LaTeX
description: Double bars with subscript 1 compute the trace norm. This diagonal matrix has singular values 3 and 4.

title: Grover search with state reflections
description: Reflect in the marked state and the initial uniform state. The leading minus preserves the diffusion convention.

title: Embed a qubit into a qutrit
description: A rectangular Kraus isometry changes the output dimension while preserving the state trace.

title: Probability of a general measurement effect
description: IBM's non-projective two-outcome example. An effect determines probability; it is not itself a Kraus operator.

title: Scalar offsets mean identity
description: In a spin expression, adding 1 adds the identity operator. This projects onto zero with weight two.

title: CUDA-Q Hamiltonian energy
description: The qBraid CUDA-Q example at theta = 0. CUDA-Q index 0 is the rightmost tensor factor, so its prepared state is |01⟩.

title: IBM root fidelity convention
description: The General Formulation course uses unsquared fidelity. Qiskit state_fidelity and this app's fidelity function use its square.

title: Optimal binary state discrimination
description: Helstrom success probability for equally likely |0⟩ and |+⟩ states. The trace norm includes the prior weights.

title: A positive matrix with negative entries
description: Positive semidefinite means nonnegative eigenvalues, not nonnegative individual entries.

title: Positive entries can be indefinite
description: This matrix has eigenvalues 3 and -1, so its positive entries do not make it positive semidefinite.

title: Check a general measurement effect
description: An effect must lie between zero and the identity in Hermitian matrix order.
